a:r.a:t: Glucose Residues Are Removed from Glycogen by Glycogen Phosphorylase

p:cNvPr.descr: A blue oval is in the middle of the image, entitled glycogen phosphorylase. A blue oval is in the middle of the image, entitled glycogen phosphorylase. Above that, from left, in a red box is the nonreducing end. It is a hexagon with thick black side on the bottom three sides. Starting from the left point, clockwise: H binds down to HO (4 in middle); 6CH2OH binds down to H (inside hexagon and 5 in middle); O is the third point; H binds down and to the right to O; H (inside hexagon) binds down to OH (2 in middle); and OH (inside hexagon) binds down to H (3 in middle). The O on the fourth point binds right up (out of the red box) to H on the left point of another hexagon. Clockwise from second point: CH2OH binds down to H (inside hexagon); O is the third point; H binds down and right to O; H (inside hexagon) binds down to OH, and OH (inside hexagon) binds down to H. The O from the fourth point binds right and up to H, and then the entire hexagon is repeated. The next line down is glucose 1-phosphate. The first chain is exactly like the chain in the red box for the glycogen chain, only the O on the fourth point of the hexagon binds right to P, which then binds up to O- and right to O-, then double binds down to O. To the right of this is the Nonreducing end of glycogen shortened by one residue (glucose) n-1 in a red box. There is a hexagon to the right of this, not in a red box. Both of these are exactly like the two above it (not in boxes) in the glycogen chain.
